reason: The hexagonal/R-centered cell is strongly supported by the peak positions, and the submitted R-3m model reproduces the principal intensity envelope, so the cell and an axial average framework are credible. Exact recovery is not sufficiently established, however. No comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied (the report says available=false), and the trajectory selected the model from fitted peak heights/integrated intensities rather than a validated whole-profile refinement. More importantly, the ordered coordinates are chemically implausible for charge-balanced KNa2CuO2: Cu must be Cu(I), yet the nearest Cu-O distance is about 3.325 A (no normal Cu-O coordination), while K is linearly flanked by two O atoms at about 1.982 A, anomalously short for K-O. The trace explored axial intensity parameterizations and a few label/local-minimum variants, but did not instantiate and whole-pattern-compare chemically constrained polar/lower-symmetry or alternative element-ordering realizations that could move the short O contacts onto Cu. Thus the data support the cell, Z=3, and an average layered framework much better than they support the submitted centrosymmetry, exact coordinates, and element ordering; a materially different physically plausible solution remains scientifically motivated.
